title: An Empirical Design Justice Approach to Identifying Ethical Considerations in the Intersection of Large Language Models and Social Robotics
findings: The paper cites prior research demonstrating that LLMs like GPT-3 exhibit persistent anti-Muslim bias. A key finding from its own study was that participants were concerned that the robot's pre-programmed guardrails and adherence to a specific set of values (disguised as neutral political correctness) would censor or constrain conversations about personal and potentially controversial topics, such as one participant's experience growing up queer within the Mormon church.

measurement_description: The paper does not use a formal benchmark. Instead, it cites previous research that identified anti-Muslim bias in LLMs (specifically, 'consistent conflation of Muslims with terrorism'). Additionally, through its qualitative co-design study, it captured participant concerns that the robot's pre-programmed guardrails would limit its ability to engage in conversations about sensitive personal topics, such as a participant's experience growing up in the Mormon church.
